summary: Environment A direct-binary proof that Phase 12 (Multi-language Whisper) compiled into the real Windows NSIS installer: the two new Tauri commands, the SUPPORTED_LANGUAGES table (English/Yoruba/Hausa/Auto-detect, no Igbo), and the JSON capability shape are all present in the shipped exe, with zero regression against every prior phase's symbol tripwires.

installer.ggmlTwoPassFixNote: First build attempt failed as expected on the known whisper-rs-sys ggml lib-name defect; the build script applied its established fix and the retry succeeded - the same harmless, unrelated build-toolchain quirk documented and handled identically in every prior whisper-enabled Windows rebuild this project has done.

symbolRegressionCheck.method: x86_64-w64-mingw32-strings cip-desktop.exe | grep -c <symbol>, run against the extracted installer's main executable
symbolRegressionCheck.tripwiresResult: All 10 counts identical to the Phase 11 baseline - zero regression. whisper_full_with_state stable at 96 for a 6th consecutive rebuild (Phase 7.3 through Phase 12).
symbolRegressionCheck.priorPhaseNote: Every prior-phase symbol checked (Production Integration, Church/User Roles & Permissions, Local Congregant Companion View) remains present and unregressed.

newSymbolsNote: Direct strings inspection confirms both new Tauri command names, the SpeechLanguageCapabilitiesDto JSON field names (currentLanguage, supportedLanguages, modelIsMultilingual), the set_speech_language rejection/success log message text, and - most decisively - the literal human-readable language names Yoruba, Hausa, and Auto-detect from the SUPPORTED_LANGUAGES table itself, proving the exact intended language set (not some other set) compiled into this binary. Igbo was independently confirmed absent - see ai/speech's own test suite (igbo_is_never_offered_as_a_supported_language) rather than a strings search, since absence-of-a-string is not itself proof of anything (an unrelated string could coincidentally be absent too); the presence of exactly the three intended names plus English's own already-tested code path is the stronger, correct proof here.
frontendTextSearchLimitation: The frontend bundle (dist/assets/index-*.js) is bundled into the Tauri resources directory, not searchable as plain strings inside cip-desktop.exe itself in the same way Rust symbols are - the new language <select> control's own UI copy was not independently string-searched in this phase, consistent with every prior phase's installer-contents-verification methodology in this project. Frontend correctness for this phase rests on npm run typecheck's success, the fresh Vite build hash, and the full 285/285 frontend test pass.
architecturalSafetyNotes: 2 new Tauri commands, zero new events, zero new migrations - no persistence at all.
SpeechEngine::set_language's default no-op means NullSpeechEngine/ScriptedSpeechEngine are completely unaffected by this phase.

Every prior-phase command (test_obs_connection, ensure_admin, operator_accounts, enable_congregant_companion, companion_snapshot) remains present and unregressed, confirming this phase's additions did not disturb any prior gate or feature.
environmentCStatus: Not yet performed. A real operator on real Windows hardware selecting Yoruba or Hausa with a real multilingual model installed, speaking in that language, and confirming both the transcript and its reported language field are correct - and separately confirming an English-only model honestly reports modelIsMultilingual: false - is required to close Environment C for this phase, exactly as for every prior phase's physicalHardwareStatement discipline.
